During the regular borough council meeting of **Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension (VSP)** on September 1, 2026, Ricky Ng-Adam addressed the council on behalf of **CAMO Subaquatique** ([camosub.ca](https://camosub.ca)) during the public question period.

This citizen presentation highlighted the vitality of underwater sports in our borough while raising key questions regarding the upkeep, reliability, and long-term sustainability of local municipal aquatic facilities.

---

### 1. Accessible Underwater Sports and Free Introductory Sessions

Ricky Ng-Adam highlighted CAMO Subaquatique's mission to promote **underwater hockey** and **underwater rugby** at the [Joseph-Charbonneau Pool](https://montreal.ca/en/places/piscine-joseph-charbonneau).

He emphasized the community-oriented accessibility of this offering: **introductory sessions are completely free**, followed by affordable membership options coming out to **less than $10 per session**. These sessions allow people of all ages and athletic backgrounds to discover unconventional underwater sports in a welcoming and safe environment ([0:15 to 0:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aYvfaArcdis&t=15s)).

### 2. Aging Aquatic Facilities and Recent Breakdowns

While recognizing the rich variety of recreational programs across VSP, the address shed light on a persistent issue: the aging state of municipal aquatic infrastructure.

Several aging pools in the borough have recently suffered from **unexpected equipment breakdowns and temporary closures**, disrupting practice schedules and community swim access ([1:30 to 1:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aYvfaArcdis&t=90s)).

Deep regrets were also shared regarding the **cancellation of the John F. Kennedy pool renovation project** due to funding shortfalls, leaving neighborhood residents without a much-anticipated modernized facility ([1:45 to 2:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aYvfaArcdis&t=105s)).

### 3. Response from Elected Officials: Lease Agreements and Multi-Level Funding

In response, **Sylvain Ouellet**, City Councillor for the François-Perreault district, and **Nadine Medawar**, Director of Arts, Sports, Parks Development, and Social Development for the borough, provided thorough explanations about the administrative and operational realities ([2:40 to 3:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aYvfaArcdis&t=160s)):

* **Shared Funding Models:** Major capital investments in aquatic facilities generally exceed local borough budgets and depend on multi-tiered financial arrangements involving the central City of Montreal, alongside provincial or federal grant programs.
* **Complex Multi-Party Leases:** Several community pools (including Joseph-Charbonneau and JFK) are located within school board or specialized institutions. Their operation relies on joint leases and agreements with school service centres, which introduces distinct legal and contractual procedures before major repairs or modernization projects can proceed.

### 4. Civic Engagement: Making Your Voice Heard for Infrastructure Maintenance

The borough officials appreciated the constructive citizen inquiry and urged residents, sports clubs, and facility users to remain engaged ([5:00 to 6:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aYvfaArcdis&t=300s)):

1. **Prompt Problem Reporting:** Immediately notify pool staff and borough services whenever equipment issues or defects arise, helping ensure prompt repairs.
2. **Prioritizing Asset Maintenance in Democratic Consultations:** Emphasize the importance of infrastructure maintenance, pool upkeep, and long-term capital renewal during public budget hearings and election cycles.

---

### Come Join Us in the Pool!

CAMO Subaquatique continues its regular practices in both underwater hockey and underwater rugby at Joseph-Charbonneau Pool. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced swimmer, everyone is welcome to try it out for free during an introductory session! To learn more about our schedule, affordable rates, and book your trial, visit our homepage at [camosub.ca](https://camosub.ca).
